reason: The primary abstract presents a vision-language model that aligns image and video representations before projection into an LLM, and evaluates visual-language task performance. It does not propose or evaluate an LLM serving, inference-efficiency, or inference-time compression technique; the described contribution is model representation/alignment and task performance, outside this run's scope.
title: Video-LLaVA: Learning United Visual Representation by Alignment Before Projection
